description: Replace terminal AgentSession events with a reusable Turn lifecycle across the Server, Runner, and Web.

tasks.title: Implement Server Turn protocol and Session migration
tasks.description: Make the Session bounded context the authoritative interpreter for Turn and Follow-up facts. Replace terminal Session state and close-specific grain operations with Turn activity, binding, current/latest Turn summaries, operation fences, Turn-keyed transcript persistence, and Session command/API contracts. Add the schema and startup migration that converts persisted transcript and Session state before new protocol traffic is admitted.
acceptanceCriteria: The Session grain accepts only canonical `turn.*` and `followup.*` execution facts, enforces stable Turn identity, per-Turn ordering, one start, at most one finish, and rejects legacy terminal event names.

Finished Turns leave the logical Session idle with its Runtime binding intact; missing bindings, unknown activity, Follow-up, Cancel, Compact, and Reset use the specified eligibility rules without changing TaskRun or AgentJob work results.

Follow-up reservations persist stable operation and new-Turn identities, atomically record admitted input facts, retain ambiguous delivery for reconciliation, and never automatically resend uncertain Runtime input.

The EF schema and startup migration convert legacy transcript/Session state transactionally, preserve history, map legacy terminal outcomes to Turns, and project unprovable in-flight execution as `unknown`.
Server unit and spec coverage exercises Turn invariants, command gates, Follow-up state convergence, legacy-event rejection, and migrated transcript state; `npm test` passes.
tasks.output: Server Session domain, transcript persistence, API contracts, and durable migration implementing the Turn protocol.
tasks.notes: Expose one versioned Server protocol contract for Runner and Web consumers; do not retain legacy event compatibility after migration.

tasks.title: Migrate Runner Turn reporting and durable delivery
tasks.description: Update OpenCode and Pi execution reporters, AgentJob execution, workflow actions, Follow-up handling, Cancel outcomes, and the shared runtime-event outbox to produce the Server Turn protocol. Version and migrate Runner outbox snapshots before delivery, preserving operation identity and converting ambiguous legacy Follow-up effects to delivery-unconfirmed without rerunning Runtime input.
acceptanceCriteria: OpenCode and Pi emit replay-stable Turn IDs and the same `turn.started`, Turn-scoped runtime facts, and `turn.finished` outcomes for Workflow and AgentJob execution.

Runner Follow-up handling emits admitted, rejected, or delivery-unconfirmed facts with the original operation and Turn identities; it never emits legacy Follow-up terminal events or re-invokes an ambiguous Runtime operation.
Cancel and failure paths report confirmed Turn outcomes only; inability to confirm Runtime stop leaves the Server able to project `unknown` rather than receiving a fabricated terminal event.

The outbox migrates persisted v1 records atomically before it becomes ready, preserves delivery ordering and acknowledgement semantics, and does not lose facts or duplicate Runtime input across crash/retry recovery.

Runner unit/spec coverage covers both runtimes, workflow and AgentJob paths, active/idle Follow-up, ambiguity, cancellation, v1 outbox conversion, and legacy-event removal; `npm run typecheck -w packages/runner` and `npm test -w packages/runner` pass.
tasks.output: Runner protocol producers and versioned outbox migration compatible with the Server Turn contract.
tasks.notes: Use the protocol-version gate supplied by T-001; do not implement a legacy fallback or dual-write path.

tasks.title: Project reusable Sessions in API and Web
tasks.description: Expose the Server's activity, binding, current Turn, latest Turn, and command eligibility projections through canonical Session DTOs and update AgentOps/read routes accordingly. Replace Web legacy event handling, transcript reconstruction, session lists, details, status displays, and controls so users see a reusable Session and its latest Turn rather than a terminal Session result.
acceptanceCriteria: Session API and AgentOps/read projections expose independent activity, binding, current Turn, latest Turn, and command eligibility; they do not expose normal Session completion, failure, or closure derived from historical Turn results.
Web canonical event types and live handlers consume the Turn and Follow-up protocol exclusively and remove handling for `session.closed`, `session.followup_completed`, and `session.followup_failed`.

Transcript, session list, detail, and composer views show recent Turn outcomes while allowing an idle bound Session to start another Turn; unknown and missing-binding states block or present the correct recovery controls.
Server route/DTO coverage and Web unit/spec coverage cover completed, failed, stopped, unknown, missing-binding, active Follow-up, idle Follow-up, and live event updates.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: Updated Session read APIs, AgentOps projections, and Web Session experience for reusable Turn-based conversations.
tasks.notes: T-003 can proceed in parallel with T-002 after the Server contract is available; it consumes canonical Server projections rather than deriving state from raw terminal events.
